findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O failure (missing file, permission error, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: Untrusted or transient filesystem state aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle
findings.fix: Return a Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and propagate the I/O error with ? or map_err

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric input or out-of-range values for the second field
findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV data (non-numeric value in the value column) causes a panic instead of a typed parse error
findings.fix: Return Result with map_err, propagate ParseIntError or map to a domain ParseError

findings.problem: as u16 performs a lossy cast from u32; values above 65535 silently truncate
findings.failure_mode: A valid 32-bit integer in the CSV silently wraps to a wrong u16 value, producing incorrect data with no error signal
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(u32_value) inside the Result chain and return an overflow error on failure

findings.problem: parts[1] is an unchecked index into a Vec<String> produced by split and collect
findings.failure_mode: A line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields (e.g. empty line or single-field line) triggers a panic at runtime
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to extract exactly two fields, or check parts.len() >= 2 with a get() guard and return an error

findings.problem: split(',').map(...).collect() into Vec<String> when only two fields are needed
findings.failure_mode: Allocates a Vec of owned Strings for every line when split_once would avoid the intermediate allocation and indexing entirely
findings.fix: Replace with line.split_once(',') and map the two resulting &str slices directly into the Record fields

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a side-effecting I/O call inside a map iterator that should be pure data transformation
findings.failure_mode: The parsing/transformation pipeline has observable side effects, breaking purity, making the function non-deterministic across runs, and contaminating the core with logging
findings.fix: Remove the println! from the map closure; logging belongs in the imperative shell layer that calls the pure function

findings.problem: parts[0] uses unchecked indexing on a Vec produced by collect
findings.failure_mode: If the line is empty, parts[0] panics at runtime
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') which returns (&str, Option<&str>) and handle the None case with an error

findings.problem: Function signature returns Vec<Record> with no error type; all fallible operations are hidden behind unwrap
findings.failure_mode: The API provides no way for callers to distinguish success from I/O failure, parse failure, or data corruption — all collapse into a panic
findings.fix: Change signature to fn load_events(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> with a domain error enum covering Io, Parse, MalformedLine, and Overflow

findings.problem: No try_reserve or bounded capacity allocation; the Vec grows dynamically without pre-allocation or allocation-error handling
findings.failure_mode: Under high event count, repeated reallocations cause latency spikes and the function cannot gracefully handle OOM — allocation failure is silently converted into allocation-induced panic via unwrap elsewhere
findings.fix: Use try_reserve on the Vec with checked_mul on an estimated line count, or accept an estimated_capacity parameter and handle AllocationError

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_events throughput or latency claims
no profiler evidence (flamegraph or perf) for allocation patterns in the parsing path
no allocation audit (e.g., dhat, alloc_counters) showing per-line memory footprint
no second-ring test or fuzzing harness targeting malformed CSV inputs (empty lines, missing fields, oversized values)
no command-line or CLI integration test proving end-to-end load behavior with real files
residual_risk: Static review only — no commands run. All four unwrap calls and the lossy as cast are unambiguously BLOCKERs. The function has no domain error type, no checked arithmetic, and no bounded allocation. Fixing the above findings to a clean Result-based API with split_once, try_from, and try_reserve would require structural changes beyond a simple patch.
